Name: core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we
Structural Path: id_stage_i.deassert_we -> CSR-operation suppression -> id_stage_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we during a denied operation can change authorization control and enable a protected action.
Justification: This control forces invalid or stalled CSR operations to READ; perturbing it can release an otherwise suppressed write.

Name: core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op
Structural Path: decoder_i.csr_op -> deassert_we gate -> id_stage_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op during a denied operation can change authorization control and enable a protected action.
Justification: The raw decoder operation classifies CSR reads and writes before suppression, so its corruption can create a protected write request.

Name: core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op during a denied operation can change authorization control and enable a protected action.
Justification: This post-suppression CSR operation is transferred toward execution and can carry an unauthorized write classification.

Name: core_i.csr_op
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.csr_op during a denied operation can change authorization control and enable a protected action.
Justification: The execution-stage CSR operation directly determines whether csr_we_int remains asserted.

Name: core_i.if_stage_i.branch_addr_n
Structural Path: if_stage_i.branch_addr_n -> fetched instruction -> decoder_i.csr_op -> core_i.csr_op -> csr_we_int
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating core_i.if_stage_i.branch_addr_n during a denied operation can change authorization control and enable a protected action.
Justification: Fetch redirection can select an unintended CSR-writing instruction and produced a measurable bounded bypass.
